title: Seasonal influenza including H1N1 (adult, India)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Categorise every influenza-like illness as MoHFW Category A (symptomatic care), B (oseltamivir without testing: high fever with severe sore throat, or high-risk group) or C (red flags: test, start oseltamivir empirically, admit). Oseltamivir 75 mg twice daily for 5 days, reduced in renal impairment; no corticosteroids.

sections.title: Recognise and categorise (MoHFW/NCDC 2019)
items: Influenza-like illness: sudden cough and sore throat with measured fever of 100.4 F (38 C) or more, onset within 10 days; often myalgia, headache, fatigue, rhinorrhoea, vomiting or diarrhoea.

Category A (mild): mild fever with cough or sore throat, with or without body ache, headache, diarrhoea or vomiting. No test, no oseltamivir; symptomatic care, home isolation, reassess in 24 to 48 hours.
Category B: B1, Category A plus high-grade fever (102 F, 38.9 C, or more) and severe sore throat; B2, Category A plus a high-risk condition. Give oseltamivir without testing; home isolation.

Category C (complicated): breathlessness, haemoptysis, altered mental state, seizures, reduced urine output, symptoms persisting or worsening beyond 72 hours, or worsening of a chronic disease; signs of tachypnoea, SpO2 below 90%, hypotension or cyanosis. Test, start oseltamivir empirically, admit.

High-risk groups: age 65 or more, pregnancy and up to 2 weeks postpartum, children under 5, chronic lung, heart, kidney, liver or neurological disease, diabetes, blood disorders including haemoglobinopathies, immunosuppression (HIV, steroids for 2 weeks or more, transplant), BMI 40 or more, malignancy.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Test Category C and hospitalised patients by real-time RT-PCR or another molecular assay on a nasopharyngeal or throat swab, ideally within 4 days of onset; never delay treatment for the result.
Molecular tests are preferred over rapid antigen tests; a negative upper-airway test does not exclude influenza in a ventilated patient with pneumonia, so send a lower respiratory sample.
Admitted patients: CBC, renal and liver function, blood gas, chest X-ray; blood and sputum cultures if pneumonia or suspected bacterial co-infection.

sections.title: Antiviral treatment
items: Oseltamivir 75 mg orally twice daily for 5 days for Categories B and C, all hospitalised patients, severe or progressive illness, and high-risk outpatients.
Start as early as possible, preferably within 48 hours of onset, but still treat hospitalised, severe and high-risk patients presenting later (benefit is seen up to 4 to 5 days after onset).
Otherwise healthy outpatients: treatment can be considered if seen within 2 days of onset (IDSA).

Renal dosing (treatment): creatinine clearance 31 to 60 mL/min, 30 mg twice daily; 11 to 30 mL/min, 30 mg once daily; haemodialysis, 30 mg after every dialysis session; CAPD, a single 30 mg dose after a dialysis exchange.
Consider a longer course for immunocompromised patients and those admitted with severe lower respiratory disease, pneumonia or ARDS.

sections.title: Supportive care and complications
items: Categories A and B: oral fluids, paracetamol, saline nasal drops, lozenges and steam inhalation; closely monitor the underlying high-risk condition.

Category C: oxygen for hypoxaemia, IV fluids, electrolyte balance, nutrition; monitor respiratory rate, SpO2 and consciousness. ICU for respiratory failure needing ventilation, haemodynamic instability or multi-organ dysfunction.

Antibiotics (as for community-acquired pneumonia, covering S. aureus) if severe at presentation (extensive pneumonia, respiratory failure, hypotension, fever), deterioration after initial improvement, or no improvement after 3 to 5 days of antiviral treatment.
No corticosteroids for influenza, influenza pneumonia or ARDS unless indicated for another reason (low-dose hydrocortisone only for septic shock). No IVIG.

Influenza ARDS: lung-protective ventilation with tidal volume 6 mL/kg ideal body weight, plateau pressure not above 30 cmH2O, PEEP titration; recruitment, neuromuscular blockade and prone ventilation if oxygen goals are not met.

sections.title: Isolation, prophylaxis and vaccination
items: Home isolation for 7 days from onset with droplet precautions; no repeat test is needed before discharge.
In hospital, isolate or cohort patients with beds at least 1 metre apart; staff use PPE and hand hygiene.
Post-exposure chemoprophylaxis: oseltamivir 75 mg once daily for 7 days after the last exposure for unprotected or unvaccinated exposed health workers and high-risk contacts during outbreaks.
Annual influenza vaccination for high-risk groups and health workers, using the composition recommended for the season by NCDC.

sections.title: Special groups
items: Pregnancy and up to 2 weeks postpartum: high risk; start oseltamivir promptly without waiting for tests, whatever the illness duration.
Immunocompromised patients shed virus longer: treat for longer and consider antiviral resistance if not improving.
Children (for paediatric carers): oseltamivir by weight for 5 days, 15 kg or less 30 mg twice daily, 16 to 23 kg 45 mg, 24 to 40 kg 60 mg, above 40 kg 75 mg; avoid aspirin (Reye syndrome).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting for PCR before treating Category C, pregnant or other high-risk patients.
Withholding oseltamivir from hospitalised patients because more than 48 hours have passed.
Giving corticosteroids for influenza pneumonia; missing secondary S. aureus or pneumococcal pneumonia.
Testing and treating every mild Category A patient, wasting tests and antivirals.

drugs.name: Oseltamivir (treatment)
drugs.dose: 75 mg orally twice daily for 5 days
drugs.notes: CrCl 31 to 60 mL/min: 30 mg twice daily; 11 to 30: 30 mg once daily; haemodialysis: 30 mg after each session. Nausea and vomiting common; take with food.

drugs.name: Oseltamivir (post-exposure prophylaxis)
drugs.dose: 75 mg orally once daily for 7 days after the last exposure

drugs.name: Oseltamivir (children, NCDC)
drugs.dose: Twice daily for 5 days: below 15 kg 30 mg; 15 to 23 kg 45 mg; 24 to under 40 kg 60 mg; above 40 kg 75 mg. Infants: under 3 months 12 mg, 3 to 5 months 20 mg, 6 to 11 months 25 mg twice daily
drugs.notes: Syrup available; CDC infant dose 3 mg/kg twice daily.

drugs.name: Paracetamol
drugs.dose: 500 mg to 1 g orally every 6 hours as needed, maximum 4 g/day
